The middle form φοβούμαι [I fear] means I am afraid.
Do not frighten your friends.

Do not be afraid at all.

fearing the will of Zeus.
fearing the thunder.

fearful, terrifying

arising from horror.

fearful to behold.

from these fearful faces.

fearful imitators.

fear.

where Wakefield proposed ψόφος [noise].

where Weil proposed οὔ μοι μελάθρων ἐλπὶς ἐμπατεῖν (ἐμπατεῖν [to walk in] also Victorius) φόβον [no hope of the halls walks in fear for me]. Similarly οὔ μοι φόβον μέλαθρον ἐλπὶς ἐμπατεῖ Ιος [no hope of the hall walks in fear for me] Klein (Literarisches Centralblatt 1873 p. 531).
where περὶ φόβῳ [with fear] since it can mean nothing other than 'because of fear', is not suitable for this passage. περιφόβως [fearfully] Portus. περιφόβοις [with fears] Joseph Klein.
Thus Porson for φοβοῦ νικῶν [fear conquering].
where in M the first hand wrote φόβου [of fear] above the line. πόνων [of toils] seems more probable.
A piercing fear stirred my mind.
You are full of fear.
My heart kicks my mind with fear.
producing fear.
fear of warlike arms,
I was lifted up by fear to prayers to the blessed ones.
I came with trembling fear.
For fear seizes my tongue with cowardice.
releasing the fear of enemies.
My heart does not sleep because of fear.
Bronze-wrought bells ring out fear.
looking with fear.
I am driven mad by fear of the word.
My mind is torn by fear.
And around my eyes is fear.
I stood speechless with fear.

Everything appears full of fear.
For fear stands by instead of sleep.
For me to go is in no way without fear.
Wordy prophetic arts bring fear to learn.
Fear holds me.
What fear turns you away?
I do not lament like a bird in a bush from fear.
No hope of the hall walks in fear for me,

35 For a piercing, bristling fear (thus Heath for φοῖβος ὀρθόθριξ [bristling Phoebus], and the scholiast reads φόβος [fear]) – sounded from the depths, falling heavily with fear upon the women in the house,
Do not hide in your heart for fear of someone.
My heart dances with fear.
